items.explanation: Hindi writer Vinod Kumar Shukla was conferred the 59th Jnanpith Award announced in 2025. Gulzar won in 2023, Amitav Ghosh in 2018, Damodar Mauzo in 2022, and Krishna Sobti in 2017, so none of them is the 2025 recipient.

items.question: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna awards announced in January 2025 included which of the following sportspersons?
options: Manu Bhaker
Neeraj Chopra
PV Sindhu
Rohit Sharma
Mirabai Chanu
items.explanation: Manu Bhaker was among the Khel Ratna recipients announced in January 2025, along with D. Gukesh, Harmanpreet Singh and Praveen Kumar, for achievements in 2024. Neeraj Chopra won it in 2021, PV Sindhu in 2016, Rohit Sharma in 2020, and Mirabai Chanu in 2018.

items.question: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, launched in October 2025, targets the development of how many districts?
options: 50 districts
100 districts
75 districts
150 districts
200 districts
items.explanation: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana targets 100 districts with low agricultural productivity and low credit disbursement, converging 36 existing schemes. The scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 and launched in October 2025, and the other district counts are incorrect.

items.question: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 in which city?
options: Rome
Paris
Athens
London
Berlin
items.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Paris hosted the Games in 1900, London in 1908, Rome in 1960, and Berlin in 1936, so none of them hosted the first modern Games.

items.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution, described by Dr B.R. Ambedkar as the heart and soul of the Constitution, provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
options: Article 14
Article 19
Article 21
Article 32
Article 368
items.explanation: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing citizens to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, which is why Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution. Article 14 covers equality, Article 19 covers freedoms, Article 21 covers life and personal liberty, and Article 368 covers amendments.

items.question: Who was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award?
options: Tarasankar Bandopadhyay
Kuppali Venkatappa Puttappa
Ashapurna Devi
Sumitranandan Pant
G. Sankara Kurup
items.explanation: G. Sankara Kurup, the Malayalam poet, was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965 for his work Odakkuzhal. Tarasankar Bandopadhyay won in 1966, Kuppali Venkatappa Puttappa in 1967, Sumitranandan Pant in 1968, and Ashapurna Devi in 1976 as the first woman recipient.

items.question: Match the organisations with their headquarters: 1. World Bank 2. OPEC 3. SAARC 4. NATO. Cities: A. Vienna B. Brussels C. Washington, D.C. D. Kathmandu.
items.explanation: The correct pairing is the World Bank with Washington, D.C., OPEC with Vienna, SAARC with Kathmandu, and NATO with Brussels. Every other option misplaces at least one organisation, such as putting the World Bank in Vienna or NATO in Kathmandu.

items.question: Arrange the following books in order of their publication, from earliest to latest: A. The Guide B. Midnight's Children C. Godan D. Train to Pakistan.
options: D, C, A, B
C, D, A, B
C, A, D, B
A, C, D, B
C, D, B, A
items.explanation: The correct order is Godan in 1936, Train to Pakistan in 1956, The Guide in 1958, and Midnight's Children in 1981. Godan predates the others by two decades, Train to Pakistan came just before The Guide, and Midnight's Children was published more than twenty years after The Guide.

items.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the original five members of BRICS?
options: Brazil
Russia
South Africa
India
China
items.explanation: South Africa is not one of the original members of BRICS. The grouping began as BRIC in 2009 with Brazil, Russia, India and China, and South Africa joined in 2010, turning BRIC into BRICS.

items.question: What is common to Satyajit Ray, Bhanu Athaiya and A.R. Rahman?
options: All won the Bharat Ratna
All won the Nobel Prize
All were born in Kolkata
All won Academy Awards (Oscars)
All worked with Richard Attenborough
items.explanation: All three won Academy Awards: Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992, Bhanu Athaiya won Best Costume Design for Gandhi in 1983, and A.R. Rahman won two Oscars for Slumdog Millionaire in 2009. Only Ray won the Bharat Ratna, none won a Nobel Prize, Rahman was born in Chennai, and only Athaiya worked with Attenborough on Gandhi.

items.question: The headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is located in which city?
options: Paris
London
Washington, D.C.
Berlin
Brussels
items.explanation: NATO is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. Paris hosted NATO's early headquarters before it moved, while London, Washington, D.C. and Berlin have never hosted the NATO headquarters.
